summary: CBS Sports guide to legal Kentucky online sportsbooks following the September 2023 launch of retail and online betting. It profiles Fanatics, FanDuel, DraftKings, BetMGM, Caesars and bet365, explains how to choose a sportsbook, and recounts Kentucky's betting history. It also covers local and nearby teams to bet on and defines common betting terms for new bettors.
one_line: A CBS Sports guide to Kentucky's legal sportsbooks, their promos and features, state betting history, local teams, and basic betting terms.
key_facts: Kentucky became the 34th state to legalize sports betting on March 31, 2023, and the 25th with online/mobile access.
Kentucky retail sportsbooks opened September 7, 2023, and online sports betting became legal on September 28, 2023.
About one month after launch, the governor announced upwards of $250 million had been wagered and roughly 500,000 mobile accounts created.
Kentucky imposes no restrictions on sports or prop bets, and it is one of 18 states allowing prop bets on collegiate athletes.
Fanatics Sportsbook earns FanCash at 1% on Straight Bets, 3% on Parlay Bets and 5% on Same Game Parlays, redeemable for bonuses or merchandise on Fanatics.com.
DraftKings' current promotion lets new customers bet $5 and receive $200 in free bets, and its rewards program favors daily fantasy players.
FanDuel does not offer a rewards program at this time, and it claims to be "America's #1 sportsbook".
BetMGM's signup offer is a $1500 risk free bet, and Caesars offers up to $1000 in bonus bets if a new customer's first bet loses.
bet365's signup offer is bet $1, get $365, and the sportsbook covers rare leagues and sports.
Kentucky Wildcats have eight national titles, John Calipari has coached them since 2010, and their 2,021-637 record is the best in college basketball history.
Louisville won the 2013 national title, has 10 Final Fours and a 1,726-874 record, and moved to the ACC in 2014.
With no Big Four pro teams in Kentucky, residents often follow the Cincinnati Bengals (Super Bowl appearance in 2021) and Cincinnati Reds (titles in 1975, 1976 and 1990).
A parlay combines two or more bets and all must win, e.g. a $100 three-leg parlay at 6 to 1 odds could win $600.
Juice, or vigorish, is the oddsmaker's tax; pricing both sides at -110 gives the book a 10% rake.
